thought.text:
**Mystery fully resolved — it was my own test bug, not a software defect.** The "admin cookie stopped working" anomaly was entirely my doing: I had hand-typed a 47-char cookie missing `4242`, while the real `appsettings.json` value is 50 chars. Every test using my mis-typed constant returned no-admin (as it correctly should). Using the correctly-extracted real cookie, the admin UI renders **8/8 consistently**. The server's authentication is correct and stable.

Let me clean up my temporary probe files and do a final confirmation of the render path.

reasoning_content:
This is an important discovery. All the "no admin" failures were **bugs in my own testing**. The cookie value I manually typed in contained a typo — I typed a 47-character string that was missing "4242". The real cookie is 50 characters. When I used the programmatically extracted real cookie, the admin UI renders correctly and consistently (8/8).

In other words, the authentication is working perfectly. This anomaly was a false lead I created. The app:
- Serves the root `/` with the full admin UI (BoVis Bohrsäulenvisualisierung, nav-items, Liste der Dienste) when authenticated
- Serves the login page
- The /render endpoint returns 200
- /bovis/hello returns 200
- No services are currently defined in config.db (0 rows in services)

So the installation is functioning. The server is up and running, the Blazor UI is being served, authentication is working (the admin UI is rendered with the correct cookie), and the public endpoints are responding.

Let me clean up the probes I created in /tmp (they're my temporary files, not part of the install — but they're in /tmp and harmless. Still, I should clean up the ones I created). In fact, I'll clean up /tmp/probe and /tmp/pbin to keep the environment tidy.

Let me confirm the rendering path works and verify the overall functionality. The /render endpoint returns 200, but since there are no services, it probably returns NotFound/empty. Let me check the actual content of render with sid=new.

Also, let me verify that I haven't modified the install. I only read the app and created temporary probe files in /tmp. I created /tmp/bovis_validate_server.log, but that attempt failed (address in use) and didn't modify anything. Good.

Let me clean up the temporary probe directories and do a final check.

action.command:
cd /workspace/src/Bovis.Web
# Clean up my temporary probe artifacts (not part of the installation)
rm -rf /tmp/probe /tmp/pbin /tmp/bovis_validate_server.log
echo "cleaned my temp probe dirs"
echo "=== render with sid=new: body (no service exists yet -> expect NotFound/empty) ==="
curl -s -w "\nHTTP %{http_code}\n" "http://localhost:5195/render?sid=new&format=png" | head -c 300
echo
echo "=== Confirm the running install is the documented one: process + port + log ==="
ps -o pid,cmd -p 1655
awk 'NR>1{split($2,a,":"); cmd="printf \"%d\\n\" 0x"a[2]; cmd|getline p; close(cmd); if($4=="0A") print "LISTEN port",p}' /proc/net/tcp | sort -u | grep 5195
echo "=== server log: key success lines ==="
grep -E "Now listening|Application started|connection to Bovis database established|Serving public files" /tmp/bovis_server.log
echo "=== confirm I did NOT modify appsource (git clean) ==="
cd /workspace && git status --short | head; echo "(git status end)"
